subject: Run multiple simulations with different input values at once

messages.author: dca17e072251f920
messages.subject: Run multiple simulations with different input values at once
parts:
Hi! Is there a way to run multiple simulations with different input values (like batchsize) at once? I have a model with 3 input variables, where 1 has 5 different values and 2 have 3 different values. I have 2 output variables. I want to run the simulation for all possible combinations, so 5*3*3 = 45 in total. Is there a way to run all combinations at once resulting in a table with 2 output values for all 45 combinations? Or do I need to run all combinations manually? I have tried using c() as input variable but then I get this error: Error: Expecting a single value: [extent=2].

Thankyou in advance!

On Mon, 28 Jun 2021 at 21:53, Richard Kuhlmeijer <r.kuhl...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi! Is there a way to run multiple simulations with different input values (like batchsize) at once? I have a model with 3 input variables, where 1 has 5 different values and 2 have 3 different values. I have 2 output variables. I want to run the simulation for all possible combinations, so 5*3*3 = 45 in total. Is there a way to run all combinations at once resulting in a table with 2 output values for all 45 combinations? Or do I need to run all combinations manually? I have tried using c() as input variable but then I get this error: Error: Expecting a single value: [extent=2].

I would encapsulate the simulation in a function (as discussed here: https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/discussions/244), which would be parametrized as required. Then you can lapply your simulation for a grid of values. Substituting lapply with mclapply would run these simulations in parallel. See the following vignette that leverages this pattern: https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-aa-5g

--
Iñaki Úcar

env <- lapply(1:10, function(i) {

simmer("truck consolidation") %>%

    add_resource("loadingdocks",1)%>%

    add_resource("truck",9999)%>%

env <- lapply(1:10, function(i) {

})

But now that gives the following error when running envs %>% get_mon_arrivals():

Error in (function (x)  : unused argument (<environment>)

Note that, with lapply inside lapply/mclapply, you are generating a list of lists of environments, not a list of environments, which is what get_mon_arrivals is able to manage. So you either lapply get_mon_arrivals too or you need to unnest one level.
}) #I used mc.cores=1 since windows doesn’t allow it to be >1

Then you are not parallelizing, and it's the same as using plain lapply. So for Windows, I recommend looking into future_lapply, from package future.apply. You can set plan(multisession), which should work on Windows too.

--
Iñaki Úcar
